title: Crowded Trades, Fluctuating Markets- Navigating the New Era of Investing - Systematic Investor 345

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Crowded Trades, Fluctuating Markets- Navigating the New Era of Investing - Systematic Investor 345.docx

speakers: Nick Baltas (co-host, QIS/systematic strategist at a bank)
Niels Kaastro Larsen (host, Top Traders Unplugged)
summary: Niels Kaastro Larsen and Nick Baltas review the April 2025 tariff shock: hedge fund positioning, why trend followers struggled with V-shaped reversals, CTA dispersion and crowding. They then discuss pension fund bond allocations, economic-trend (macro data) signals versus price trend, and a Man Group paper on trend's behaviour before and after equity peaks. Conclusions: trend works in sustained drawdowns and not in sharp reversals, dispersion comes from speed and market differences, and new signals need caution beyond backtests.

coverage.note: information overflow and systematic approach; client topics, rates and equity concentration
hedge fund net vs gross exposure, crowding, QIS tactical timing, natgas curve trades, single-decision-maker regime
historical presidential shocks and decade of no returns; information bursts and V/W-shaped markets
every crisis feels new; gold inflation-adjusted and long-term asset returns
elite universities raising cash, private equity liquidity, QIS as liquidity, risk vs uncertainty
pension funds' bond allocation, risk-free assets rethink; trend barometer
April 2025 trend challenges by sector, commodities reliability, synchronous reversion and speed effects
fast vs slow programs; signals crossing zero; April 2025 index returns
longer-term trend reducing vs flipping; Denmark 1807; question on dispersion and autocorrelation
drivers of dispersion, CFM blog, short vs long-term correlation
autocorrelation of trend returns, switching costs; equity crowding Mag7
crowding in trend portfolios; trend barometer percentile; credit QIS question
credit QIS challenges; economic trend discussion begins
economic trend mechanics, regime slowness, gold/bonds role, risk of missing equity trends
IPM cautionary tale, backtests flatter; Man Group paper intro and Kaminski contrast
trend followers as price takers; when trend works; Man paper pre-peak period

completeness_estimate: 0.90 - core ideas (V-shaped reversals, dispersion drivers, correlation by horizon, economic trend, Man paper) all captured; missed some positioning/sector details, the career-risk explanation of bond-heavy pensions, PE smoothing and the 2025 economic-trend performance; one measure conflated.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastro Larsen
claims.quote: I mean if you weren't rules based I would imagine that this is probably impossible uh really to make sense of right.
claims.claim: A rules-based approach lets investors cope with information overflow in volatile news-driven markets, which discretionary investors cannot process.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: they started adding shorts rather than cutting the longs and that is not necessarily the behavior that you end up seeing in these type of events.
claims.claim: Prime brokerage data show hedge funds cut net exposure sharply from February to April 2025 while gross stayed high, since they added shorts rather than cutting concentrated longs.
claims.indicator: hedge fund net and gross exposure (prime brokerage data)

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: Do they drive performance? Yes, they do. Are you rewarded from holding them? Maybe you are.
claims.claim: Crowded positions drive performance but whether holding them is rewarded is uncertain, so how to treat crowding remains debated.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: there could be some possibilities specifically in the V space that becomes a bit more stretched at times to to create signals or at least suggest that the market is more appreciative of um of an entry point.
claims.claim: In QIS, stretched volatility (or value) conditions could provide tactical entry signals, although tactical timing is hard.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: It was colder than expected. Inventories were actually quite shallow. So some of the curve trades were impacted by that.
claims.claim: In winter 2024-25 a colder-than-expected season and shallow inventories disrupted natural gas curve trades, prompting discussion of forming spreads more dynamically.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastro Larsen
claims.quote: perhaps the first time really where a single person can move the markets to the extent that the markets are moving at the moment and I don't know that there is a model for that
claims.claim: Markets are driven by one decision-maker's announcements and no model exists for that.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastro Larsen
claims.quote: Both of those led to a decade or or so uh with no returns for equity investors.
claims.claim: Presidential policy shocks (Nixon's 1971 dollar devaluation; Hoover's 1930 tariffs) were each followed by roughly a decade of no equity returns, raising the question whether current tariff policy could do the same.
claims.indicator: US equity decade returns after policy shocks
claims.conditions: Large trade or monetary regime changes

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: whether it's a single person or a single entity, information flows now very quickly in bursts.
claims.claim: Information now arrives in bursts through social media and text/NLP processing, so tariff announcements and reversals produce V- or W-shaped moves driven by sentiment.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: primarily driven by emotional reaction more so than I guess driven by by by by by financial valuation
claims.claim: Large daily swings (futures up 5-8% then reversed) are driven by emotional reaction rather than valuation; recession forecasts were revised and reverted within three days.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastro Larsen
claims.quote: if we go back 50 years as trend followers there will been many times where we would have felt that at the time um and then things get kind of more normal again.
claims.claim: Every crisis feels unprecedented in the moment; over 50 years of trend following similar feelings occurred and markets normalised.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastro Larsen
claims.quote: gold is only now back at the peak level on an inflation adjusted basis um to what it was in 1980.
claims.claim: Gold's real price has only just returned to its 1980 peak, so it did not preserve real value over 45 years.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastro Larsen
claims.quote: Um and gold has been you know 5.12% for the very long period 5.42% for the very long period and 8.3 uh 03% since 2015. But equities have been somewhat better.
claims.claim: Gold returned about 5.1-5.4% for long periods and 8% since 2015 but equities did slightly better, so gold's reputation as a great investment is overstated.
claims.indicator: long-term gold vs equity returns (Damodaran table)

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastro Larsen
claims.quote: they are trying to get rid of some of that ill liquid stuff now.
claims.claim: Elite US universities (Princeton, Northwestern, Yale) issuing bonds and trying to sell illiquid private holdings shows the liquidity downside of private assets.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: QIS can can play a role um that can perhaps act as a as a liquidity resource also to finance some of the some of the calls some of the capital calls
claims.claim: Liquid QIS strategies can act as a liquidity reserve to fund private-equity capital calls.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: risk and uncertainty can be perceived as equal notions, but one is measurable and manageable and that is risk that's volatility.
claims.claim: Risk (volatility) can be measured and managed; uncertainty (the unknown) cannot, which is the challenge investors face.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastro Larsen
claims.quote: I don't really see if gold didn't beat inflation, then bonds certainly didn't beat inflation.
claims.claim: Long-term evidence shows bonds failed to preserve real value, yet some pension funds (80% bonds in places, sometimes leveraged) still hold them.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastro Larsen
claims.quote: do we need to think about safe havens, risk-free investments, etc., etc., in a completely different way than we have been for a long time.
claims.claim: Recent US bond behaviour questions the 'risk-free' status of Treasuries and calls for rethinking safe havens in pension portfolios.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastro Larsen
claims.quote: doing a little bit better during this uh during this um turbulence uh turmoil
claims.claim: Shorter-term trend strategies did better during the April 2025 turmoil; the trend barometer at 50 was okay.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastro Larsen
claims.quote: it just looks like that commodities as a sector tends to be very reliable and pretty reliable through all of these types of of crises
claims.claim: Commodities are the most reliable trend-following sector across both short and long crises; energies were the best sector in April 2025.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: Uh so not only do you need to revert your signal kind of it allows you to to get into the new positioning and then boom uh the reversion comes through.
claims.claim: Medium-speed trend models need days to reduce and reposition, so a V-shaped drop and rebound hits them twice (reduce then re-add).

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the reversion that we have seen across the markets in a synchronous manner was the more challenging part
claims.claim: In April 2025 equities, dollar, oil (OPEC) and yields all reverted at once, a broad reshuffling that left trend followers caught off guard.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: some of the faster programs point in time they had less of an initial drop but they somehow now continue kind of bleeding.
claims.claim: After the April 2025 reversal, faster programs lost less at first but kept bleeding, while slower ones lost more first and then caught up, so differences in speed produce different paths.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: It was like almost everything met each other at zero.
claims.claim: After the reversion many trend signals crossed zero together, so it was unclear whether the resulting positioning is just rounding or a new trajectory.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastro Larsen
claims.quote: The beta 50 I mean these not these numbers are not uh very bad. Um down 3.86% uh in in April, down 3.91% in year to date.
claims.claim: April 2025 (to Apr 29) returns: Beta50 -3.86% (YTD -3.91%), SG Trend -5.15% (YTD ~-10%), Short-Term Traders -0.41%, Bridge flat-fee trend -6.27%, MSCI World -2.5%, S&P 500 -4.13% (YTD -8.23%), US Agg -1%.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastro Larsen
claims.quote: at least for the longer term trend followers it's probably more about reducing positions but not necessarily flipping positions right now.
claims.claim: In April 2025 longer-term trend followers cut positions rather than flipping them.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastro Larsen
claims.quote: even if you're actually at war with someone after a couple of decades I think it lasted then suddenly things change again.
claims.claim: Alliances and tensions between countries can revert, as the 1807 British bombardment of Copenhagen shows, so current geopolitical ruptures may normalise.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: speeds probably the most important one. Uh markets and type of markets that manages our trading. Uh static versus dynamic positioning that's a third one which is quite important.
claims.claim: Return dispersion among trend managers comes from (1) speed, (2) markets traded, (3) static versus dynamic positioning, (4) core trend versus other signals such as carry, and (5) discretionary risk reductions.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: partly because we have seen some uh some significant reversions taking place and this is precisely when those choices matter
claims.claim: Dispersion has grown because large reversions (SVB, August 2024, April 2025) are when speed and design choices matter and managers have differentiated post-2022.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastro Larsen
claims.quote: they said no there's no more dispersion today than there's always been
claims.claim: CFM's blog finds no more dispersion among trend managers than historically; the result depends on which managers and horizon are measured.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: I think the more trend managers you look at the closer they would be the more CTA like the the bigger the dispersion just by design.
claims.claim: Measured dispersion depends on the number of managers; a broader set looks more CTA-like and has a larger dispersion by design.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: long-term correlation between CTAs is actually relatively elevated but short-term is not.
claims.claim: Trend managers are highly correlated over the long run but not over the short run.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: if 80% of the time you observe trends and these are the times that signals would generally agree however fast or slowterm correlation is relatively higher
claims.claim: Long-term correlation is higher because most of the time trends exist and fast and slow signals agree, while differentiation arises only around reversion points.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: I'm not too convinced that there is autocorrelation in following returns.
claims.claim: Chasing the best-performing trend speed or manager is not clearly valuable since autocorrelation of trend returns is doubtful beyond prolonged strong trends.
claims.conditions: Prolonged strong trends may show some

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastro Larsen
claims.quote: giving up on your loss carry forward every time you you make that switch
claims.claim: Switching between trend managers loses loss carry-forward (high-water marks) and fees, hurting performance.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: you ended up having very low realized correlation between stocks purely because of this divergence between the the very high cap and the rest of the universe
claims.claim: Concentrated Mag7/AI crowding in 2024 kept realised stock correlation low through divergence between mega-caps and the rest; the concentration has eased with new shorts since mid-February 2025.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: it's actually hard to claim that there is a single bed.
claims.claim: Beyond gold, there is no single crowded bet in the trend world.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: gold is by far outsized. Maybe coffee and cocoa and silver.
claims.claim: Gold is by far the most outsized trend position, with precious metals, coffee and cocoa intensifying but not concentrated.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: Depending on your speed, you're long, you're short.
claims.claim: Equity index positions net out across managers because different speeds disagree, so no crowding.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: for us like bottom quintile just to give you a sense so like it's around the 20th percentile so it's it's not significant
claims.claim: The trend barometer is at the 20th percentile of its history (low trendiness), implying reshuffling and a balanced risk allocation.

correction.issue: Conflates two measures: the 20th-percentile (bottom quintile) trendiness reading is Nick's own firm's measure; Niels' trend barometer finished at 50.
correction.fix: Nick Baltas: his own trendiness measure sits around the 20th percentile of its history (bottom quintile), indicating heavy reshuffling and a fairly balanced risk allocation across asset classes; Niels' barometer read 50.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: it was primarily historically a space that the index world as in the the CDX the the CDS indices were more utilized which obviously reduces substantially the I guess the breadth.
claims.claim: Credit QIS has been mostly index-based (CDX), which reduces breadth versus equities.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: and I think to me the challenges are primarily driven by liquidity, data validity as well as data history for back testing purposes.
claims.claim: Growth of credit QIS faces constraints in liquidity, data validity, history and costs, although more assets keep being indexified.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: there are limits to arbitrage. Maybe on paper you can observe returns but in practice getting hold of them has a clear roadblock and that being the costs right in some respect.
claims.claim: Observed paper returns are not always capturable because of transaction costs (limits to arbitrage).

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: macro regimes do not change as quickly as prices do.
claims.claim: Economic trend signals avoid day-to-day shocks because growth and inflation regimes move slowly, adding value during price corrections.
claims.testable: yes - compare economic and price trend

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: binary one and then some sort of risk adjusted by V would be enough to get you to something that looks like an economic trend behavior
claims.claim: Economic trend is implemented as a directional binary signal from growth/inflation, then volatility-scaled, going long assets expected to do well in the regime and short the others.
claims.direction: long assets that fit the regime, short others

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: what becomes more challenging is to have some sort of um sizing considerations that go beyond risk.
claims.claim: Sizing beyond risk (such as growth level) is the hard part of economic trend.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: then from an economic standpoint surprise surprise gold has a key role to play in this environment uh depending on inflation dynamics bonds have a role to play
claims.claim: With falling growth and undecided inflation, economic signals favour gold, bonds (inflation-hedged or not), possibly steepeners, and no equities.
claims.direction: long gold, bonds, steepeners; avoid equities

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: over the last year or two with negative growth in the data you would have missed quite a substantial amount of return that some of those equity trends have delivered for for CDAS.
claims.claim: Economic trend signals with negative growth would have missed equity trend returns of CTAs, so economic data is not a panacea over price trend.
claims.conditions: Equity bull market despite weak growth

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastro Larsen
claims.quote: performance stopped suddenly um and eventually uh like after a year or so they went out of business completely.
claims.claim: IPM, a Swedish systematic macro fund using economic data, raised most investor money, then performance stopped and it closed within a year, a caution for new strategies.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastro Larsen
claims.quote: even if they've been around for five or 10 years, it's still not a very long time because things keep changing, things keep evolving
claims.claim: Five to ten years of history is too short to trust newer strategies given evolving markets.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastro Larsen
claims.quote: if CTAs today were to show their uh back tested version of their current models, they would look a lot better than what the real history is.
claims.claim: Backtests flatter strategies: backtested versions of CTAs' current models would look better than real histories, so backtested papers (including replication) cannot be relied upon.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: clearly specifically that comes post a rally you're not positioned for it.
claims.claim: When the S&P falls sharply after a rally, trend followers are not positioned for it, per Kaminski's analysis.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: But should those movements become sustained and the draw down continues deeper and longer, this is when trend following starts operating.
claims.claim: Trend followers are price takers: they profit when equity drawdowns are sustained (dotcom, GFC, 2022).

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: Whereas Volmageddon or April this year or August last year or SVB, you name it, are not the environments that trend following is
claims.claim: Sharp V-shaped events (Volmageddon, SVB, August 2024, April 2025) are not environments where trend following works.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: if we go 3 months prior to S&P started dropping, trend following is just trying to reinvent itself.
claims.claim: The Man Group paper shows trend does not earn money in the three months before the equity peak either, as positions reshuffle.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: It doesn't seem to be performing a few weeks or a months post the draw down, which is Katie's work.
claims.claim: Trend also does not perform in the first weeks to a month after the drawdown starts; performance appears only if the drawdown becomes sustained.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: So these are a few examples whereby S&P is prior to hitting its peak where trend following is kind of resuffling itself
claims.claim: November 2021 and August 2007 are examples where trend was reshuffling positions before the S&P peak.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: European equities have been significantly outperforming obviously some of the defensives and the geopolitics playing out
claims.claim: In early 2025 (by mid-February, when markets priced five US rate cuts) the long-standing US-over-Europe equity pattern reversed, with European equities significantly outperforming, linked to defensives and geopolitics.
claims.indicator: US vs European equity relative performance; priced Fed cuts

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: even if at times it can kind of smooth out the volatility but doesn't necessarily deliver return
claims.claim: Private equity smooths reported volatility but may not deliver returns, so investors look to hold liquid investments alongside it, both as a hedge against weaker PE returns and as a response to US funding pressure on endowments.
claims.indicator: private equity reported volatility vs returns
claims.conditions: PE returns below history; funding shocks

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: We're talking about carrier risks that um those asset owners are supposed to be taking if and so they deviate from those policy portfolios.
claims.claim: Asset owners keep bond-heavy policy portfolios despite poor long-run real bond returns partly because deviating from the policy portfolio carries career risk.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: not only equities have not necessarily delivered return, not only nominal but you know even even sorry not only real but also nominal
claims.claim: Japan is a case where equities failed to deliver even nominal returns for long periods and asset owners leaned on fixed income, which the recent yield rise has hurt.
claims.direction: bond-heavy allocations hurt by rising yields

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastro Larsen
claims.quote: equities, currencies, some fixed income markets to a smaller degree have been the most challenging
claims.claim: In April 2025 the hardest sectors for trend followers were equities, currencies and to a lesser degree fixed income, with precious metals and copper also under pressure.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: some of the more DM markets are now I guess on the long side kind of shorting the
claims.claim: Over April 2025 trend positioning in currencies shifted to long developed-market currencies versus the dollar, and energies were modestly short, but neither is a crowded trade.
claims.indicator: trend positioning in DM FX and energy
claims.direction: short USD vs DM FX; mild short energy

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastro Larsen
claims.quote: for example in a year like this year uh those type of signals have done very well
claims.claim: Economic-trend signals (built on macro data rather than prices) have done very well in 2025, though they are relatively new with limited live history; AQR runs roughly a 50/50 mix of economic and price data.
claims.testable: yes - compare economic vs price trend returns 2025
